C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2.Summary: Repair the `--flush` mode's `--decision` path in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`. A selected decision currently mints its index `Entry` and never its `Decision` element, so `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --flush … --decision D41 …` exits **0**, prints `record-flush: flushed D41`, leaves `rulings.xml` byte-unchanged and writes an orphan index row (`<Entry id="d41" token="D41" genre="decision" layer="live" />`); the record's three validators — `validate-record-retirement.ts`, `validate-citation-anchors.ts` and `prove-record-preservation.ts` — all report green on that state. This bundle makes a `--decision` selection land as a `Decision` element and its index `Entry` together, makes the verb refuse any selection it would not write (`flush-selection-genre-mismatch`) so the success line never names a token the record does not carry, and adds the general index-versus-genre presence invariant: the at-rest relation `record-index-orphan` through the shared structural check (validator, `--retire`, `--flush`) and the pre-write relation `flush-index-orphan` over the flush's own next-documents — the class guard that would have caught this instance and would not be reached by the adjacent `F277` layer check. It pays `F289`; at the close the authority flushes `F289` and the held decision `D41` (the ruling that hand-editing a run stream is ungoverned and forbidden) through the repaired verb, then archives and retires in one wave. Minted 2026-09-18 as `C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2` from slug `RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH` on branch `c-record-decision-flush` at base commit `a104166b2034bb06e028598b6533c9becaeccdfb`; `ngrace spec new RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH --timestamp 2026-09-18T00:06:40Z` printed `mint: C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2 slug=RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH lineage=1 hash=368E01F2 branch=c-record-decision-flush timestamp=2026-09-18T00:06:40.000Z` and `mint-search: 0 active, 0 archive prior bundle(s) share slug RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH` — whose value half, `0 active, 0 archive`, is this bundle's dogfood `--mint-search` input, carried verbatim because a recomputed count is not the mint-time fact. Searched before minting, 2026-09-18 at `a104166b2034bb06e028598b6533c9becaeccdfb`, over `.ngrace/changes/archive/` (121 directories) and both registry layers for any prior bundle carrying `RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH`: no directory and no row carries the name. The predecessor `C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A` (archived, merged in `2434fd4`) built the `--flush` mode this bundle repairs; its plan named a decision selection and its delivered suite drove only a finding (see `Problem`).
C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2.Problem:
**`F289` is the defect, re-measured rather than inherited.** Driven 2026-09-18 on a whole-repository copy at `a104166b2034bb06e028598b6533c9becaeccdfb` with a fixture active bundle, the shipped verb `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --flush docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH --change <fixture> --decision D41 --mint-search "0 active, 0 archive"` exits **0** and prints `record-flush: flushed D41 (row <fixture>, pays )`. The record disagrees: `grep -c d41` over `rulings.xml` returns **0**, `rulings.xml`'s live root is byte-unchanged at `<Rulings base="1670" headroom="213" ceiling="1883">`, `findings.xml` is byte-unchanged, and `decisions.xml:421` carries `<Entry id="d41" token="D41" genre="decision" layer="live" />` — an index line asserting a live decision that exists in no genre file. The same index-plus-no- element state is produced by `--decision F289` (a finding token) and `--finding D41` (a decision token): each prints `record-flush: flushed F289` / `flushed D41`, exits 0, writes the row and no entry at all.
**The cause, read from the engine and corrected against the brief's paraphrase.** In `flushRecord` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1523`), `selF` filters buffer entries of genre `finding` by `--finding` tokens (`:1536`), `selD` filters genre `decision` by `--decision` tokens (`:1537`), `nextFindings` appends the rendered `selF` elements (`:1588`), `nextIndex` appends index entries for **both** `selF` and `selD` (`:1589`), and `nextRulings` is initialised to the unchanged `rulingsXml` (`:1595`) and rewritten only inside `if (opts.codify)`. No path appends a selected decision's element. **A `Decision` renderer does exist**: `renderDecision(entry, status)` (`:437`), the same shape as `renderLiveFinding` (`:1514`) — `id`, `token`, `status` attributes with `Title` and `Body` children, plus optional `CodifiedIn`/`TaughtIn` (declared in `scripts/record-serialize.ts:64`–`77`) — and the flush never calls it. The brief's hypothesis "no equivalent renderer exists for a `Decision`" is **wrong**; the asymmetry is in `flushRecord`'s composition, not in the renderer inventory. That correction matters because the fix is to route `selD` through the existing `renderDecision(e, "live")` and append it to `nextRulings`, not to mint a parallel writer.
**The second report-without-doing path is in the same selection contract, and it is measured.** The pre-write presence check is `for (const id of [...opts.findings, ...opts.decisions]) if (!parsed.entries.some((e) => e.token === id)) throw flush-id-absent` (`:1529`–`1531`), which checks only that the token is in the buffer, never that the flag's genre matches the entry's. So a token under the wrong flag survives to the success line (`:1633`, which prints `[...opts.findings, ...opts.decisions]`) with `selF`/`selD` empty. This is a distinct instance of `Summary`'s second property ("cannot report what it did not do") and is repaired by one genre-agreement refusal.
**Why no shipped guard caught the orphan.** `assertRecordSchema` validates each next-document in isolation, so an index with a row and a rulings file without the element are each well-formed on their own. `structuralCheck` (`:1475`) builds its `holding` map from the findings and rulings pairs and skips every index `Entry` whose id is not in it — the guard is `if (expected && expected !== node.attributes.layer)` (`:1498`–`:1500`), so a missing holding is silently green. `validate-citation-anchors.ts` checks the inventory-to-index direction only (`:153`–`:168`) and `prove-record-preservation.ts` checks inventory-to-index too (`:66`–`:84`); no shipped check consumes the index-to-genre direction. Driven on the F289-produced copy, all three shipped validators exit 0 (`record-retirement: ok`, `citation-anchors: ok`, `record-preservation: ok`), and `validate:ci` is green over a record that points at nothing.
**Why the predecessor's suite was green without driving a decision.** The approved predecessor spec's `AC-FLUSH-MODE` (`C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A`) words the criterion "the selected finding **and decision** each exist exactly once across their genre pair", and its plan's T-002 pass criterion repeats "flushes the selected finding and decision". The delivered suite (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:6262`–`6355`) drives `--finding F999` only; no test anywhere passes `--decision` to `--flush` (the fixture decision exists solely as the `--codify` target). A criterion naming a decision was green without any decision being selected — the plan asserted a mechanism it did not exercise, and `bun test` could not see the gap. This is recorded as the shape of the miss, not as a second defect to pay here; the repair is that this bundle's suite drives `--decision` in both directions.
**Why the two held entries cannot move until this lands.** `D41` — the maintainer's ruling that hand-editing a run stream is ungoverned and forbidden, not a precedent until the PILOT decision — is staged in the gitignored buffer `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` and can reach `rulings.xml` only through the `--decision` path that mints an orphan today. `F289` is staged beside it. The authority caught the orphan by parsing the record rather than trusting the printed confirmation and reverted the uncommitted flush; had it committed, the only repair would have been a hand edit of the record, which `D41` itself forbids. Recovery was available only before the commit.
**What is deliberately unchanged.** Every record write stays behind the module-private `writeRecordXml` and the all-or-nothing validate-then-write transaction. The engine stays under `scripts/`; no `src/` production file changes (`D40`'s boundary). No ceiling is raised (`D39`); no root attribute is hand-written. The buffer is read, never written, by the verb and by this bundle. `README.md` and `examples/` are unchanged. Escaping of markup in XML artifacts is mandatory character-data form (`<`, `>`, `&`), never paraphrased brackets.

Goals.Goal: **Symmetry: a `--decision` selection writes its element and its index `Entry` together.** In `flushRecord`, route every `selD` entry through the existing `renderDecision(e, "live")` and append those elements to `nextRulings`, so the shipped `--flush` writes the `Decision` into `rulings.xml` exactly once and its index `Entry` into `decisions.xml` exactly once, with `status="live"`, `genre="decision"` and `layer="live"` agreeing — the same transaction, the same `writeRecordXml` path, the same root re-derivation the finding path already uses. A `--codify` in the same run applies its `CodifiedIn` to the already-appended `nextRulings`, never to the original bytes, so a flush that selects decisions and codifies cannot drop either write. This is the instance fix for `F289`.

**Report honesty: the verb cannot report what it did not do.** A `--finding` token whose buffer entry is of genre `decision`, or a `--decision` token whose buffer entry is of genre `finding`, refuses with the named code `flush-selection-genre-mismatch`, exit non-zero, **before any write** (all four record files byte-unchanged). The success line continues to print the flushed tokens, and every token it names is carried by the record. The existing refusals — `flush-id-absent`, `flush-id-duplicate`, `flush-row-not-active`, `flush-row-exists`, `flush-pays-unknown`, `flush-charter-f-token`, `flush-status-text-f-token`, `flush-status-closed-with`, `flush-codify-absent`, `flush-codify-exists`, `flush-mint-search-malformed`, and the serializer's `record-schema-*` — are unchanged.

**The class guard: the index-versus-genre presence invariant, in both directions of evaluation.** One relation — *every index `Entry` has a holding genre element of its own genre in one of its pair's two layers* — evaluated (a) **at rest** by the shared `structuralCheck`, as a new code `record-index-orphan`, consumed by the validator (`validateRecordRetirement`), by `--retire` (through `refuseStructural`) and by `--flush` (through the same `refuseStructural` at the top of its transaction); and (b) **before the flush's write loop**, over the in-memory `nextFindings`/`nextRulings`/`nextIndex` documents the flush is about to persist, as the named code `flush-index-orphan`, so a flush that would mint an orphan refuses before any write. This is the general invariant the brief asks this bundle to decide: it catches the whole class, not this instance, and it is the presence half that complements `F277`'s layer half (the layer agrees in the F289 state, so `F277`'s check cannot fire). The production record satisfies the relation and stays green.

**Pay `F289`, and land `F289` and `D41` through the repaired verb at the close.** The bundle's charter row (`--change C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2`) carries `Pays` naming `F289`. At the close, with the bundle still under `.ngrace/changes/active/`, the authority drives one `--flush --change C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2 --finding F289 --decision D41 --pays F289 --mint-search "0 active, 0 archive"` through the repaired verb, then the gate apply and `--retire` run in one wave. `--retire` moves `F289` (its `PaidBy` names this now-archived bundle) and the row to the retired siblings and flips their index `Entry` layers in place; `D41` lands `status="live"` with no `CodifiedIn` and stays live (a live decision is eligible only with a resolving `CodifiedIn`). This bundle is the first `--decision` user, which is why the flush is a close act rather than left to a later bundle.

**No regression in the existing contract.** The finding path, the codify-only invocation, the all-or-nothing property (a refused run leaves findings, rulings, index and registry byte-identical), the held ceilings, the canonical-at-rest property, and the buffer's read-only treatment are unchanged and re-driven by the suite. The one measured fixture consequence of Goal 3 is repaired inside this bundle: the `C-ROOT-WINDOW` fixture (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:956`) reassigns `parts.findingsRetired` to a finding `f9` while `parts.index` keeps `happyParts`' `<Entry id="f2" … />`, leaving `f2` unheld; with the new relation in place that fixture would red, so its index and retired-finding bytes are made consistent.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier **T1 (module change)**. The deliverable is one existing engine file and its suite: no new subsystem (the `--flush` mode and its transaction shipped in `C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A`), no new graph module, no version surface, no `src/` production file. T1's full `strict_contract` sections are met and no design-freeze note is owed. Roadmap `RM-GOVERNED-PATH`.

Binding rulings carried, not re-derived. **`D27`** — approved artifacts are immutable and repaired only by `ngrace supersede`; drafts are revised in place, and this spec is a draft. **`D30`** — the record freezes for the lifetime of a bundle that measures it, and no hard `Constraint` here transcribes a scalar count of a file it changes; every occupancy and root figure lives in `Assumptions` and expires. **`D31`** — the retired sibling is a layer; the index has no retired sibling, so eligible `Entry` layers flip in place. **`D39`** — no ceiling is raised; every root write is the held splice. **`D40`** — the record is written by the verb under `scripts/`; no `src/` production write. **`D41`** — hand-editing a run stream is forbidden; this bundle does not touch a run stream and does not relax the prohibition, and its own record writes are the verb's.

The vehicle and the boundary. The whole fix lives in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, a mode/check of the record engine beside `--retire`, `--stamp-paid-by`, `--rewrite-roots`, `--split` and `--flush`. Every record write stays behind the module-private `writeRecordXml` and the module-private renderers; the fix reuses `renderDecision`, adds no exported writer and no second renderer. The new validator code `record-index-orphan` and the two flush codes `flush-selection-genre-mismatch` and `flush-index-orphan` are record-engine codes, **not** `src/lint/catalog.ts` issue codes — no lint issue code is added and `src/` is untouched. The verb is invoked as `bun …`, never `ngrace …`. `package.json` is unchanged: `record:flush` already exists and `validate:ci`/`validate:record-retirement` still contain no mutating mode.

The selection contract. `--finding <token>` and `--decision <token>` are matched by anchor token against the buffer entries; **the flag's genre must equal the entry's genre**, or `flush-selection-genre-mismatch` refuses before any write. The default `Pays` remains the flushed `F` tokens in buffer order; `--pays` overrides and may name a flushed token or a live finding's token. The row's name is the `--change` bundle id checked against `.ngrace/changes/active/`; its `kind` is `chartered`; `Number` is empty. The buffer is read whole, never written. The output line prints the flushed tokens, the row name and `Pays` (and, for the codify-only invocation, the codified decision), and every token it names is present in the record after the run.

The invariant, as one relation with two evaluation points, and its measured cost. The relation is *an index `Entry` has a holding `Finding`/`Decision` of its genre in one of the pair's two layers*. At rest it is part of `structuralCheck`, so `validateRecordRetirement` reports `record-index-orphan` and exits non-zero, and `--retire`/`--flush` refuse through the existing `refuseStructural` before any write, with no second implementation. Before the write loop the flush evaluates the same relation over its in-memory next-documents and refuses `flush-index-orphan`. The relation is driven in both directions on throwaway copies; the production record satisfies it (measured 2026-09-18: 419 index `Entry` elements, 263 live, 0 orphans). The measured fixture cost is the `C-ROOT-WINDOW` fixture's orphan `f2`, repaired in this bundle. The reverse direction — a genre element with no index `Entry` — is not this relation and stays the province of `validate-citation-anchors.ts` and `prove-record-preservation.ts`; this bundle does not widen it.

The transaction and the dogfood, and what the authority writes. One transaction: all four next-documents are built in memory, each checked by `assertRecordSchema`, the index-versus-genre presence relation checked over them, every live root's base re-derived from the shipped metric read back, each persisted ceiling held byte-for-byte via the `--rewrite-roots` splice, and only then written through `writeRecordXml`; a refused run writes nothing. This bundle's full-suite-run count is **zero**: no `CloseEvidence` names the whole suite, and the whole-suite `bun run validate:ci` is a close drive in `VerificationIntent` only. **Acts assigned to the authority, with their write targets declared:** at the close the authority drives the single `--flush --finding F289 --decision D41` invocation, which writes `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml`, `rulings.xml`, `decisions.xml` and `registry.xml`; then the gate apply (which renames the bundle into `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2/`); then `--retire`, which writes `findings.xml`, `findings-retired.xml`, `rulings.xml`, `rulings-retired.xml`, `registry.xml`, `registry-retired.xml` and `decisions.xml`. The authority composes the `--charter` and `--status-text` halves (neither names an `F` token; the `StatusText` carries no `Closed with` sentence). The authority prunes the buffer only after the flush PR merges.

Write scope, anchors and modules — enumerated once (`F136.1`'s rule; no second module list anywhere in this artifact). The set is every write a Goal makes inevitable: `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` (the `renderDecision` routing into `nextRulings`, the `flush-selection-genre-mismatch` refusal, the `record-index-orphan` relation and the `flush-index-orphan` pre-write check); `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the decision-path walks both ways, the genre-mismatch refusal both ways, the orphan relation's validator/`--retire`/`--flush` directions, the `C-ROOT-WINDOW` fixture repair, this bundle's row and flush relations); the record files `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/{findings.xml,findings-retired.xml,rulings.xml, rulings-retired.xml,registry.xml,registry-retired.xml,decisions.xml}` (the close flush writes the first, third, seventh and fifth; the close `--retire` writes the rest); and the bundle's own artifacts under `.ngrace/changes/active/C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2/` with their close arrival under `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2/`. `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md` is the stub and is not written; `record-inventory.json` is `--split`'s artifact and is not written by the flush or by `--retire`. **No graph module is written or minted.** `isModuleOwnableWritePath` was run and returned `false` for `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` and `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` and `true` for `src/grace-cursor.ts` and `src/artifact/xml.ts`; neither scoped file carries a `LINKS:` header, so no module is forced into `AffectedAreas` and the later plan's `DurableScope` will be `<None />`. The record files under `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/` are owned by no module in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml`; `M-RELEASE-AUTOMATION` owns the six contract-bearing release scripts, not this engine. Do not add a `LINKS:` header to a record-engine script. `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is read, never written. `README.md`, `examples/`, `package.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/plans/README.md`, `src/` and `skills/` are not touched.

Evidence hygiene. The byte-invariance baseline is the full base commit `a104166b2034bb06e028598b6533c9becaeccdfb` (`F210`'s rule: the base-less diff form cannot fail). `git diff` sees tracked paths only (`F174`). Every `CloseEvidence` command is evaluated in the applied-archive state (`F196`) and additionally driven inside a faithful whole-repository copy before and after these criteria were written; exits are read directly, never through a pipe. Every criterion states a relation and pins no projected figure; any occupancy or root number lives in `Assumptions`. Structural counts come from the shipped parser, never `grep -c`. Any test this bundle adds that walks the real repository or the real archive runs under `bun run test` (`bun test --timeout=0`); **no per-test timeout number is pinned** (`C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2`), and the CI job's `timeout-minutes` is the only ceiling. The full `bun run validate:ci` is a close drive, never a `CloseEvidence`.

The rule this repository has now paid for four times (`F136`, `F282`, `F285`, `F286`), applied. (a) For every value the deliverable moves or renames, the tree is grepped for its assertions and the grep's findings are scoped. This deliverable moves no token, id or path out of the record; it adds codes and reuses `renderDecision`. Known boundary, stated rather than hidden. (1) The presence relation covers the index-to-genre direction only; the genre-to-index direction stays `validate-citation-anchors.ts`'s and `prove-record-preservation.ts`'s. (2) `--decision` continues to require a buffer entry whose anchor token matches; the verb never invents an element from a flag alone. (3) The `flush-index- orphan` check is a tripwire over the flush's own output; with the symmetry fix it cannot fire on a correct run, which is the point. Owner: unchanged; no user-visible surface — the verb is a `scripts/` meta-artifact of this repository's governance and never a shipped `ngrace` command, so the marketplace-facing overview and the walkthrough project have nothing to learn.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DECISION-LANDS:
On an isolated fixture root with a fixture buffer and a fixture active bundle, `--flush --change <fixture> --decision <D> --mint-search "0 active, 0 archive"` writes a `<Decision>` element into `rulings.xml` exactly once and its `<Entry>` into `decisions.xml` exactly once, `status="live"`, `genre="decision"` and `layer="live"` agreeing; the `--finding` path is unchanged; findings, rulings, index and registry each satisfy `base + headroom = ceiling` with `base` equal to the shipped metric read back; each written file is canonical at rest (`serialize(parse(file))` byte-equal to `file`); the buffer's sha256 is unchanged; and the run's success line names the decision token. Failure: `rulings.xml` byte-unchanged while the index gains the `Entry`; the printed token absent from the record; a non-canonical byte; a written root that does not hold its ceiling. The instrument is the shipped suite.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REPORT-HONEST:
A selection whose flag disagrees with the buffer entry's genre refuses before any write: `--decision <a finding token>` and `--finding <a decision token>` each exit non-zero with `flush-selection-genre-mismatch`, and findings, rulings, index and registry are byte-identical (sha256 before equals after). No run exits 0 with a success line naming a token the record does not carry. Both directions are driven on a throwaway copy: the clean selection passes, the mismatched selection reddens with the code in the message. Failure: exit 0 with the row written and the named token absent (the measured F289-adjacent path); a refusal that writes before refusing; a code that fires on the clean fixture. The instrument is the shipped suite.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INDEX-PRESENCE:
The index-versus-genre presence relation is enforced in both evaluation directions and both probe directions. **At rest:** a planted index `<Entry>` whose id has no `Finding`/`Decision` in either layer makes `validateRecordRetirement` report `record-index-orphan` and exit non-zero, and makes `--retire` and `--flush` refuse through `refuseStructural` before any write. **Before the write:** a flush that would mint an orphan index `Entry` refuses `flush-index-orphan` before the write loop, leaving all four record files byte-identical. **Both ways:** the clean fixture and the production record satisfy the relation (`validate-record-retirement: ok`); the F289-produced state driven on a whole-repository copy — an index `Entry id="d41"` with no decision element — now reddens `record-index-orphan` where `validate-record-retirement.ts`, `validate-citation-anchors.ts` and `prove-record-preservation.ts` all exited 0 before. The `C-ROOT-WINDOW` fixture's orphan `f2` is repaired so the suite is green with the relation in place. Failure: a planted orphan left green; a refusal that writes first; the relation red on the production record. The instrument is the shipped suite.
